strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with clone
strategies.desc: Uses 8 sequential all-reduce operations with explicit clone() calls between each stage, performing local scale/unscale operations in loops over W shards. Results in 8 all-reduce dispatches plus 8 clone dispatches (16 total). Baseline approach with no fusion, highest dispatch count but clearest dependency chain.

strategies.name: Fused local-ops per all-reduce
strategies.desc: Eliminates clone() by using in-place tensor slicing and pre-allocated buffer reuse, fusing scale and divide operations into single-pass loops. Reduces to 8 all-reduce dispatches plus minimal buffer management. Trades memory safety for dispatch reduction by reusing buf tensor across iterations.

strategies.name: Batched scale coefficients vectorized
strategies.desc: Precomputes all scaling coefficients as a tensor, then uses broadcasted element-wise operations instead of loops over shards, enabling kernel fusion. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but local operations become single vectorized multiply/divide ops per stage. Lower dispatch count through vectorization at cost of temporary coefficient tensor.

strategies.name: Pipelined two-phase all-reduce waves
strategies.desc: Splits the 8 iterations into two groups of 4, overlapping the local computation of group N+1 with the all-reduce communication of group N where dependencies allow. Requires careful buffer orchestration but can hide ~50% of local-op latency. Same 8 all-reduce dispatches but improved wall-clock through pipeline parallelism.

strategies.name: Hierarchical reduce-scatter then all-gather
strategies.desc:
Replaces each all-reduce with reduce-scatter (producing W/k partitions) followed by local processing then all-gather, exploiting the fact that each rank only needs its shard result mid-pipeline. Results in 16 collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but with smaller per-dispatch payload (1/k of full vector), trading dispatch count for bandwidth efficiency at large W=224.
